answer: At the dawn of an agent economy, a spiral of verification costs forms a protective reef against Sybil attacks. Agents must stake escalating compute resources on each new identity, verified by a checkable rule where the hash of the agent's unique behavioral trace must match a public challenge derived from prior interactions. This forces attackers to incur real, cumulative costs for every fake identity, as each spiral layer demands unique, non-reusable proof of ongoing engagement that cannot be batch-generated without proportional expense.
